entities.name: UNC1878

entities.name: Wizard Spider

entities.name: FIN6
entities.evidence: Active since 2015, FIN6 traditionally targeted point of sale (POS) terminals and eCommerce payment servers in order to exfiltrate and resell banking data.

entities.name: TrickBot
entities.evidence: Emotet-TrickBot-Ryuk, TrickBot-Ryuk and Bazar-Ryuk are not the only infection chains leading or having led in the past to the deployment of the Ryuk ransomware.

entities.name: BazarLoader

entities.name: Buer
entities.evidence: Buer loader was used to gain a foothold in an intrusion where Ryuk was deployed [38].

entities.name: SilentNight
entities.evidence: SilentNight is also involved in attacks aimed at distributing Ryuk ransomware.

entities.name: Emotet

entities.name: More_Eggs
entities.evidence: TerraLoader had installed the backdoor More_Eggs

entities.name: Conti
entities.evidence: After emerging in December 2019 [43], the Conti ransomware is believed to have been made available to affiliates based on a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) model.

entities.name: Maze
entities.evidence: Conti, which unlike Ryuk has a dedicated site for the disclosure of data stolen from victims, even published the data of two victims listed on the Maze dedicated leak site.

entities.name: LockerGoga
entities.evidence: From mid-2018, technical and operational evidence suggests that FIN6 or affiliated parties were distributing the Ryuk and LockerGoga ransomware (which appeared in January 2019).

entities.name: TerraLoader
entities.evidence: it was found that during infection chains involving PowerTrick and Anchor, TerraLoader had installed the backdoor More_Eggs

entities.name: Zloader
entities.evidence: SilentNight is also involved in attacks aimed at distributing Ryuk ransomware. This trojan, sold on Russian-speaking underground forums since the end of 2019, is a variant of the Zloader malware (from the ZeuS source code) whose last activity dates back to 2018 [39].

entities.name: FrameworkPOS
entities.evidence: the editors Morphisec [41] reported intrusions in early 2019 in India, Japan and the United States into POS systems belonging to the financial and healthcare sectors, using Cobalt Strike and the FrameworkPOS malicious code.

entities.name: More_Eggs
entities.evidence: the attackers are believed to have used PowerShell to download and execute TerraLoader, in turn responsible for installing More_Eggs, a method specific to FIN6 according to IBM
